script.title: Why Sulla Chose Fire Over His Family's Grave

lines: Rome carried its dead dictator on a golden litter, then burned him.
Two thousand gold crowns stood for the offices he held in life.
His name was Sulla, and the year was 79 BC.
By then, most Romans burned their dead.
But Sulla's noble family still buried their dead in the ground.
Sulla was the first of them cremated.
Sulla may have feared that Marius's supporters would deface his body.
You see, it's like shredding a secret note instead of just throwing it away.
But burning a body was hard work.
A good pyre used about half a cord of timber.
Someone had to tend the fire for 8 or 9 hours.
Without enough wood or skill, bodies were left part-burnt, like Pompey's.
After the fire, the heir sprinkled the ashes with wine.
He gathered them into an urn and buried it.
Yet even ashes could be attacked.
The emperor Caracalla took his brother Geta's ashes.
He mixed them with the ashes of executed men, as a final insult.

claims.claim: The dictator Sulla, given a funeral at public expense, was carried on a golden litter, with two thousand gold crowns to represent his offices in life.

In the Mid- to Late Republic cremation became the most common burial practice; patrician members of the gens Cornelia continued inhumating their dead until 79 BC, when Sulla became the first patrician Cornelius to be cremated.
Sulla was cremated perhaps because he feared his body would be defaced by supporters of his arch-enemy, Gaius Marius.
An effective pyre used about half a cord of timber and had to be tended for 8 or 9 hours; the unplanned cremations of Pompey and Caligula left their bodies part-burnt for want of fuel or skill.
After a cremation, the heir sprinkled the ashes with wine, gathered them, placed them in an urn and interred them.
Caracalla deliberately mixed the ashes of his brother Geta with those of his executed supporters, as a final insult.

cast.sulla: a 60 year old Roman dictator, heavy build, a pale blotchy reddish face, short thin white hair, a heavy jaw, clean shaven, cold pale blue eyes, a white toga with a broad purple border, 1st century BC
cast.marius: a 70 year old Roman general, wiry build, a deeply tanned wrinkled face, close-cropped iron grey hair, a hooked nose, a bronze muscled breastplate and a dark crimson cloak, 1st century BC
cast.undertaker: a 45 year old Roman undertaker, broad shoulders, a shaved head, a thick black beard, a sleeveless rust orange wool tunic and a stained leather apron, 1st century BC
cast.heir: a 22 year old Roman nobleman, slim build, thick black curly hair, a thin beardless olive face, a plain dark grey mourning toga, 1st century BC
cast.caracalla: a 25 year old Roman emperor, stocky build, short tight black curls, a short dark beard, a deep scowl, a gold-trimmed purple cloak over gilded bronze armour, 3rd century AD
